endorsements.quote: AI users should regularly monitor and update models to detect evidence of drift in performance over time, as well as across different populations and settings.
Healthcare organizations: Assess AI model performance in the context of local patient populations and use cases before deployment
Develop transparent consent processes to inform patients about the use of their data in AI applications.
Include explanations of risk-based data collection strategies, highlighting how only the minimum necessary data will be collected and used based on risk assessments.

A monitoring program must be implemented to detect and assess the validity of a tool’s output or validity given RWD's ongoing and changing input, based on the metadata standards and transparency framework proposed above.

These frameworks and labels should document data sources, algorithms, evaluation results, and known limitations, recommended use cases, and any known limitations, particularly concerning potential applicability in differing contexts of use or populations such as in Sendak 20

Metadata standards should be established from existing standards under the same Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable (FAIR) principles 12 recommended to characterize RWD sources, including provenance, context of creation, collection methods, coverage (ie, geographic, temporal, socio-demographic representativeness), and formats.
Develop accessible educational materials on the potential benefits, risks, and limitations of RWD-driven AI in healthcare.
Provide a clear description of accountable responsibilities from each stakeholder group’s perspective.
All RWD considered for use in developing AI applications should be carefully evaluated in terms of both known and potential biases, particularly with respect to the intended context of use.
AI developers should Implement bias detection and mitigation strategies during model development and validation.

unlisted_practices: Require pre-specification of protocols for use of RWD and RWE to ensure rigor and transparency in development, testing, validation, and implementation of AI tools.
Re-train or re-validate an existing AI tool against appropriate RWD before applying it to a different population or clinical context.
Data providers should document known limitations to the representativeness of their data.
Standards development organizations should develop metadata standards and standards for collecting socio-demographic patient and population characteristics.
Foster ongoing multi-stakeholder dialogue, including patients and advocacy groups, to align AI development and deployment with societal values and patient needs.
Regulatory bodies should define guidelines for periodic audits and updates of adaptive AI systems and require documentation and approval of re-validation efforts.
Developers should evaluate candidate datasets for fitness for the intended use before developing AI.
Develop educational materials for patients, caregivers, and the public on how AI in their care may benefit or harm them and how their data may be used.
Require clear consent protocols and robust anonymization techniques to protect patient privacy in RWD-based AI.
Use common data models such as OMOP to harmonize RWD across sources.

screen.reason: Expert consensus panel providing recommendations and framework guidelines for the responsible use and governance of real-world data and AI in healthcare.
